body:
## Problem

After #593 (PR #619), the fold checks that the base holds a gone branch's merged head by ancestry (`git merge-base --is-ancestor <merged head> <base_ref>`). A stack PR merged by **squash** or **rebase** leaves no such ancestor, so the fold now stops with "merged somewhere other than <base>" (iteration-6 carry-forward: "Squash/rebase merges now stop here too; that is fine (out of scope)"). PR #619 lists it as not covered and the docs say merge commits are required. No issue tracks it.

Repos that only allow squash merges can't use stack mode across a merge.

## Done when

Decide whether stack mode supports squash/rebase merges (e.g. compare the merged PR's tree or patch-id instead of ancestry) or refuses them up front with a clear message at publish/merge time rather than at the next fold. Document the choice and pin it with a test.

Found by the eduralph/pdca-pdca Act review of 2026-10-02 (issue_593 iteration-v6 carry-forward + PR #619).

comments.body:
One more case for this issue's decision, from #652 (PR #670):

PR #670 spreads "not clean" from every reason in the carry's `why`, and that includes the `edge` case. The `edge` case is a PR that is MERGED but whose head is on neither the base nor the line (`_finished_head`, `flow.py:854-856` on #670's branch). A squash or rebase merge produces exactly that state. So a finished Q that depends on a squash-merged P is now held with the `built_on` advice: "get issue_P carried, or re-drive issue_Q on a base without it" (`flow.py:866-867`). P's work *was* reviewed and merged, so that advice points the wrong way. Before #670, Q was carried.

Whatever this issue decides (support squash/rebase, or refuse it up front), the cascade should match it. Either an `edge` hold doesn't cascade, or the hold's advice says that P was merged by squash/rebase and what to do. Pin it with a test for a MERGED-not-on-base P with a finished dependent. No test covers that today.

Found by the eduralph/pdca-pdca Act review of 2026-10-10 (issue_652 §6/§10).
